The Argand diagram above shows the roots of a cubic polynomial $f(x).$
Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $-5.$

$f(x)=$
{{field-1}}${x}^{3}\,+$
{{field-2}}${x}^{2}\,-$
{{field-3}}$x\,+$
{{field-4}}
worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=3$ and ${x}_{2,3}=\pm 2\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-5.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =-5(x-3)(x-2\text{i})(x-(-2\text{i})) \\  & =-5(x-3)(x-2\text{i})(x+2\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-5(x-3)(x-2\text{i})(x+2\text{i}) & = \\ -5(x-3)({x}^{2}+x(2\text{i})-x(2\text{i})-(2\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ -5(x-3)({x}^{2}+4) & = \\ -5({x}^{3}+4x-3{x}^{2}-12) & = \\ -5{x}^{3}+15{x}^{2}-20x+60.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=-5{x}^{3}+15{x}^{2}-20x+60.$
